Have you ever overcome a fear of something?
Fear of sex. Probably one most people are scared of before their first time.

I don't think fear would be an accurate description of my first time. But I definitely had a lot of butterflies. It felt a lot more like a first day of school, where there's this dichotomy of excitement about exploring new territory and an uncertainty of how to act and what to say. I, however, was fortunate enough to have been exposed to comprehensive sex-education instead of the horrors of abstinence-only education. If one had the misfortune of enduring the latter, then I could totally see fear as being a justified emotion. Should this have been the case for you, fear not, because Last Week Tonight with John Oliver has you covered (or uncovered)!

Public speaking.

I thought about it and practiced. I realized that the audience wasn't rooting for me to fail, they wanted to hear what I had to say. I'd spent so many months researching, learning, becoming an expert at whatever it was, and they wanted to know what I knew. They wanted me to succeed.

With that in mind, it became much easier. I knew that when I got in front of people, they thought of me as the man. It just became a matter of going for it, and after a few times I became better. Now...getting in front of a room full of execs is not a problem, talking to room of hundreds is easy.

Public speaking seems to be a pretty common fear. There's a joke that Jerry Seinfeld does about how more people fear public speaking than they fear death, which means that if they were to go to a funeral, they'd prefer to be the person in the casket over the person giving the eulogy.

A few. My first was heights. I still get a sense of vertigo sometimes by being at the edge of something. I decided that I should just try to enjoy being safely scared, and did things like ropes courses. Had a fabulous time once with a damn wasp flying around me while I was in the middle of a difficult crossing, and I realized I'd spontaneously started singing "If I Can Learn To Do It" from Anastasia, something I hadn't thought about in years. Still fear those goddamn wasps though. Now I enjoy a mild unease with heights. Someday I hope to jump off a cliff and swing across a canyon. I'm sure I'll practically pee my pants but I bet it'll be a wonderful rush.

The other was driving, especially in strange places. I didn't actually get my license until after college. Then I finally got a job, but it was 45min to an hour's commute. That helped a lot, except the driving in new places anxiety. One of my New Year Resolutions one year was to destroy a fear, so I wrote down all the ones I could think of that I had and rated them. It seemed like an easy one to conquer, so I started visiting friends who lived further away, taking excursions, etc.

I still haven't completely conquered my fear of spiders, but now I usually find them cute. It's only the large ones, in person, that make me very nervous. Fuck roaches and wasps though. Bees aren't as bad as I thought, but wasps are evil.
